title: Wordmark Color Usage
slide_intent: Limit wordmark colors by context so the name stays connected to core brand recognition while signs remain fabricable.
strategic_value: Primary-color lettering and a controlled light reversal can keep the Burger King name coherent across print and signage.
demonstration: Three large wordmarks show Fiery Red, Flaming Orange and BBQ Brown on pale; two light versions sit in a brown block, with the white version labeled restaurant signage only.
practical_value: Use primary palette colors or Mayo Egg White reversal, and handle fabricated signage with the specified white material and softer lighting.

reference_purposes.Constraint: Wordmark use is limited to primary palette colors and the specified reversal; fabricated acrylic/plastic signage uses white with softer lighting to emulate Mayo Egg White.

ingredient.name: Wordmark color
ingredient.role: Keep the name within the core identity palette.
ingredient.application: Use Fiery Red, Flaming Orange or BBQ Brown; reverse in Mayo Egg White from a primary color.
ingredient.scope: Historical guide; acrylic/plastic restaurant signage uses white material and softer lighting to emulate Mayo Egg White.
